The following table sets forth our results of operations and the amount of change between the periods indicated. The period-to-period comparison of financial results is not necessarily indicative of future results.

Selling, general and administrative. SG&A expenses increased by $14.1 million, primarily due to higher legal and consulting costs of $4.7 million related to merger and acquisition activities, increased stock‑based compensation of $4.2 million, and higher employee‑related costs of $3.1 million associated with increased headcount as we expanded our organizational infrastructure. The increase was further driven by other costs of $2.1 million.

Research and development. R&D expenses increased by $12.6 million, primarily due to higher development costs of $5.4 million and increased employee‑related costs of $3.7 million, reflecting higher headcount and stock‑based compensation. The increase was further driven by legal costs of $1.8 million, facility and insurance costs of $0.6 million, and other costs of $1.1 million.

Amortization of intangible assets increased by $1.4 million due to intangible assets acquired in connection with the acquisition of Less Common Metals.

rd.text: We own and operate a fully automated and instrumented hydrometallurgical demonstration facility at our Wheat Ridge, Colorado research and development center that was commissioned in June 2026 and commenced production of separated rare earth oxide samples in July 2026. We also own and operate Less Common Metals Ltd. (“Less Common Metals”), a metal-making facility located in Cheshire, United Kingdom, one of the few commercial producers outside of Asia with the capability to convert rare earth element and critical mineral oxides into metals and alloys. Additionally, we own and operate a rare earth magnet manufacturing facility in Stillwater, Oklahoma (“Stillwater Facility”). The Stillwater Facility was commissioned in the first quarter of 2026 and began NdFeB magnet sales in the third quarter of 2026.

Our effective tax rate of 8.3% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 differs from the statutory tax rate of 21% due to changes in valuation allowances in the United States and Switzerland, foreign tax benefits generated on current year losses, and recurring permanent differences and discrete items that may occur in any given year, but are not necessarily consistent from year-to-year.

net.text: Our revenues for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were derived primarily from our metal-making operations and our neo magnet manufacturing production. We incurred a net income of $11.7 million and a net loss of $68.3 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively. Our historical results are not indicative of our future results, and our ability to generate sufficient revenue to achieve profitability will depend largely on the successful development and scaling of our integrated mine-to-magnet platform and our global value chain.

ocf.text: We expect to continue to use cash in our consolidated operating activities for the foreseeable future as we invest in commercializing our integrated mine-to-magnet platform. Our primary near-term uses of cash include:

capex.text: The amount and timing of our capital expenditures is within our control and subject to management’s discretion. We retain the flexibility to defer a portion of planned capital expenditures depending on a variety of factors, including, but not limited to industry conditions, increased costs, delays in project development, the availability of necessary equipment, infrastructure and capital, capital needs of other strategic initiatives and market conditions. Our goal is to allocate our capital to advance our objectives and maximize returns.

profile.name: USA Rare Earth, Inc.
profile.category: Non-accelerated filer · Smaller reporting company · Emerging growth company

intro.text: USA Rare Earth, Inc.’s mission is to be a global leader in the supply of critical minerals and advanced materials and the partner of choice in producing rare earth elements, oxides, metals and magnets. Rare earth elements and critical minerals are vital inputs to end markets including national security, technological innovation, and the increasing number of advanced manufacturers who seek a reliable source of rare earth materials and magnets. We intend to deploy capital in effective and efficient ways to develop our assets and to deliver innovative, high-quality products to our partners and customers. We are building an integrated rare earth mine to magnet value chain that we project will be resilient through economic cycles, and well-positioned to meet today’s market dynamics and national security priorities.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: The Carester investment, when completed, has an aggregate estimated value of €40.0 million, or approximately $45.3 million.

If the investment is completed, the platform will unite the technological expertise, process innovation, and production capacity of our manufacturing operations and those of Carester with the goal of accelerating development and strengthening our capabilities across the rare earth value chain.

Our efforts to realize anticipated benefits and synergies from our acquisitions, including our pending minority investment in Carester SAS, our acquisition of Texas Mineral Resources Corp. (“TMRC”) and the Serra Verde merger are complex processes and may disrupt our operations if not implemented in a timely and efficient manner and could adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
